prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, and has knee injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1285; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported in Katy, Texas. Can you state your full name for the record?

A: Sure. I'd rather not put my full name on this, if that's okay. Just call me the driver of the blue sedan.

Q: That works for the file. Can you walk me through what happened?

A: I was heading down the two-lane road, going maybe twenty-five miles an hour. A pickup came over into my lane while it was passing a slow truck. I hit the brakes and steered right, but we still clipped front to front. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jerk me forward.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, and the airbag didn't deploy, which I was glad about.

Q: Did you hit anything with your body inside the car?

A: My right knee slammed into the dashboard below the glovebox. It hurt right away and it's been swollen since. I got out and could walk, but it was stiff and I felt pain when I put weight on it.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same afternoon. They took X-rays and told me nothing was broken, but I have a follow-up with an orthopedic doctor next week because the knee still locks up sometimes.

Q: Did you have any problems with that knee before this collision?

A: No. I'd been running regularly and had no knee trouble at all.

Q: Is there anything else you want to add?

A: Only that the other driver admitted at the scene that they didn't see me coming. I'd like the claim handled so I can get my knee treated without a lot of delay.

Q: Thank you. I'll note that and follow up with you about the medical records.
